messages.author: 7d04014e6f57d1be
messages.subject: BioGeoBears GenSA test in RASP (Reconstruct Ancestral State Phylogeny)
parts: Hello, thanks for accept me. I try run a analisys in RASP 4.1.2. and the manual recommend first run a test in BioGeoBears. RASP package come with GenSA and I start the test. I left de computer run for 72 hours and the test make little (if none progress). That is normal? Or I'm doing some thing wrong?

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] BioGeoBears GenSA test in RASP (Reconstruct Ancestral State Phylogeny)
parts:
Hi -- I've never tried running BioGeoBEARS via RASP so I don't know what they've done. I would recommend just running the example script:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

...that should make the problems more obvious. Most likely issue: you have too many areas, so the state space is huge, so the likelihood calculation fills up the memory on the computer, so you never get through 1 likelihood calculation, let alone the ~1000 that GenSA requires. But that's just a guess.

Cheers!
Nick

parts:
Had the same problem and informed Yan Yu. He promptly answered and also uploaded a new version of RASP, which works fine!

You can now choose between GenSA and optimx for the implemented BGB analyses.
